title: Politics, Book I
author: Aristotle
license: public domain (Jowett translation, 1885; via MIT Internet Classics Archive)
notes: Book I whole, chapters 1-13 (MIT labels them 'Part'). Project Gutenberg was down for maintenance, and its Politics (#6762) is the Ellis translation, so Jowett was taken from the MIT Internet Classics Archive.

title: Oeconomicus (The Economist)
author: Xenophon
license: public domain (Dakyns translation, 1897; Project Gutenberg eBook #1173, via the xmission PG mirror)
notes: Whole dialogue, chapters 1-21, with Dakyns's footnotes as '> [n]' quote lines after the paragraph that cites them. Fetched from the xmission Project Gutenberg mirror (gutenberg.org was down for maintenance).

title: Oeconomica, Book I (the household)
author: Pseudo-Aristotle
license: public domain (Forster translation, Oxford 1920, published before 1931; scan via Internet Archive)
notes: Book I only (chapters 1-6: household, wife, slaves, the householder); Book II (finance anecdotes) left out as off-topic. Forster did not translate 'Book III'. OCR of the 1920 Oxford edition, hand-checked against the scan text: marginal Bekker line numbers and running heads removed, footnotes dropped except the Hesiod and Aristotle cross-references (kept inline as [note: ...]); chapter headings carry the Bekker page where each chapter starts.

title: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
author: Sir Robert Filmer
license: public domain (1680; EEBO-TCP Phase I, CC0)
notes: 1680 first edition, whole: Heylyn's letter + chapters I-III. Each chapter's printed argument comes first, then the numbered sections (n) as headings. The 1680 printing misnumbers some sections in ch. III (12 and 15 twice, no 11 or 14); kept as printed. 17th-century English royalist rather than ancient, filed under classical as requested. EEBO-TCP keyed transcription (TEI XML from the textcreationpartnership GitHub mirror; quod.lib.umich.edu was behind a bot challenge). Long s normalised; marginal notes inlined as [marg.: ...]; TCP illegibility marks (•, 〈◊〉, 〈…〉) and '〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉' kept as in the transcription. Filed under English custom: an English work on patriarchal government.
